body:
## Summary

Given a real repository coding task, Formal AI's agent mode does not attempt the task. It writes a
plan file, `cat`s it back, and reports success — leaving the working tree untouched. Repeating the
run reproduces the identical no-op every time.

This is the failure behind
[link-assistant/hive-mind#2130](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2130)'s `agent`
run, and it is the concrete instance of what #848 measures in aggregate ("no level where Formal AI
can write code yet"). Filing separately because there are two specific, fixable defects visible in
the trace rather than a general capability gap.

## Evidence

Task: solve a "hello world" issue in a freshly generated repository. Log:
[`agent-18-V7E0Ee.log.gz`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-2130/data/tool-logs/agent-18-V7E0Ee.log.gz).

The plan Formal AI emitted, in full:

```text
step 1
  capability "Write"
  action "append the bounded repository work-item plan to .formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino"
step 2
  capability "Run"
  action "read back the persisted work-item plan"
  command "cat .formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino"
verification_command "cat .formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino"
```

and the closing message:

> Recorded and verified the bounded repository work-item plan for `…/issues/1`.
> The deterministic sandbox preserved the requested goal without claiming unobserved source edits.

No source file was written. The harness restarted the run and got the identical no-op five more
times before stopping at its restart limit.

### Defect 1 — the task is reduced to writing a plan about itself

Both steps operate on `.formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino`. The `verification_command` reads back
the file the run itself just wrote, so verification passes by construction and carries no
information about whether the *request* was satisfied.

The wording is careful not to claim work it did not do, which is the right instinct and traceable to
the honesty fix in #843. But the run still **terminates as though the request had been served**. A
plan that contains no step touching the requested artefact should not reach a success terminal state;
"I produced a plan and could not execute it" is a different and more useful outcome than "recorded
and verified".

### Defect 2 — the `goal` field is the caller's entire system prompt

```text
general_change_plan
  id "repository_work_item_plan_2e20e5283d3e8ce1"
  execution_mode "repository_work_item"
  goal "You are an AI issue solver using @link-assistant/agent.\nGeneral guidelines.\n
        - When you execute commands and the output becomes large, save the logs to files…
        - When running sudo commands, especially package installations, run them in the background…
        - When a code or log file has more than 1500 lines, read it in chunks of 1500 lines…
        […the whole preamble, several KB…]"
```

The objective — *solve this issue* — never lands in `goal`. What lands there is the operating
instructions the harness prepends. Everything downstream that reasons about the goal is therefore
reasoning about CLI etiquette, which plausibly explains why the planner concluded the task was
"record a work item".

The same pollution shows up in the recovery ladder for `claude`, where the retry prompt's `Request:`
line is built by joining raw argv:

```text
Request: --output-format stream-json --verbose --dangerously-skip-permissions --model formal-ai
  --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config /tmp/…/mcp.json --disallowedTools AskUserQuestion … -p Issue to solve: …
```

so the two are one bug wearing two hats: **the request is taken from the raw input rather than from
the parsed prompt.**

## Reproduction

```bash
git init /tmp/fa-repro && cd /tmp/fa-repro
echo "PROMPT" > /tmp/p.txt   # any issue-solving prompt with a system-prompt preamble
cat /tmp/p.txt | formal-ai with agent --model formalai/formal-ai
# → .formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino is created; no other file is
# → the plan's `goal` field holds the preamble, not the objective
```

Environment: formal-ai 0.317.0, agent 0.25.5.

## Suggested fix

1. **Separate the goal from the preamble.** Take the objective from the parsed prompt — for a
   harness-driven run that is the task text, not the operating instructions. If the two cannot be
   told apart, the boundary should at least be explicit (a documented delimiter, or a dedicated
   argument) rather than "everything the caller sent".
2. **Reject self-referential verification.** A `verification_command` whose only effect is to read a
   file the plan itself wrote proves nothing. Require the verification to observe an artefact named
   in the request, and if no such artefact can be named, end in a "planned, not executed" state
   instead of a success state.
3. **Do not report success for a plan with no step touching the request.** This preserves the #843
   honesty guarantee while removing the part that misleads the caller — the terminal state.

## Related

- Downstream: link-assistant/hive-mind#2130
- Aggregate measurement of the same gap: #848
- Honesty fix this behaviour is built on: #843
- Wrapper argv defects found in the same investigation: #902, #903
- Full analysis: [case study §3.2](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-2130/README.md)
title: Agent mode reduces a repository coding task to writing a plan file and `cat`-ing it back, then reports success — and the plan's `goal` is the caller's system prompt
